subject: RE: Term & Renewal language - cadence, notice windows, and TFC proposal
body_plain:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Pike <jordan.pike@procureco.com>, procurement@procureco.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Term & Renewal language - cadence, notice windows, and TFC proposal

Jordan / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion, I put together a short proposal that we think gives ProcureCo the runway you want for planning while keeping an operational guardrail for both sides. Key pieces are:

- Auto-renew: standard 12‑month renewal term if neither party provides notice; renews on same term and pricing in effect unless an agreed amendment is executed.
- Notice window: we propose a 30‑day out notice for non‑renewal for customers on annual terms; for pilots or short-term orders (<=3 months) propose 14 days.
- Termination for convenience (TFC): allow either party to end with a 90‑day notice and a TFC fee that phases based on remaining committed months (see attached TFC_fee_table.csv).
- Offboarding SLA / data exit: Redwood provides a 45‑day retrieval window with export assistance; additional retained snapshot upon request (see draft order form).

We want to surface two optional concessions if you need them: 1) extend notice window to 60 days for enterprise orders > $250k ARR, or 2) convert TFC into a pro‑rated service credit (instead of cash fee) for customers with active renewal discussions. Either concession would be scoped to the Order Form and not change the MSA baseline.

Attached: Redwood_MSA_v3_markup.pdf (redlines called out for §3 Term, §4 Auto‑Renew, §7 Offboarding), OrderForm_ProcureCo_DRAFT.xlsx, and a TFC fee table.

Next steps: if you can confirm which concession (if any) you need, we’ll route a clean MSA + Order Form for signature; otherwise we can accept your redlines and iterate.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Lead, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

-----
From: Jordan Pike <jordan.pike@procureco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@procureco.com, legal@procureco.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 14:30:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Term & Renewal language - cadence, notice windows, and TFC proposal

Ben —

Appreciate the clear writeup and attachments. A few items from our side:

1) Notice window: our standard procurement team asks for 60 days for renewals on annual agreements. Is 30 days the firm ask from Redwood? If so, can we scope 60 days as an enterprise exception (you hinted at this) and include a revenue threshold?

2) TFC fee: the concept is reasonable but we prefer a cash-free route. Can Redwood consider a pro‑rated credit instead of a cash fee? If not, we need the exact calculation and cap.

3) Data retention/offboarding: 45 days is acceptable, but need a clause guaranteeing transfer assistance and an export format (S3 compatible).

We’ll also run this by legal and send redlines if anything else looks off.

Jordan Pike
Director, Procurement | ProcureCo
jordan.pike@procureco.com

-----
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Pike <jordan.pike@procureco.com>, procurement@procureco.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:01:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Term & Renewal language - cadence, notice windows, and TFC proposal

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick reply. Short answers first:
- Notice: we can accept 60 days as an enterprise carveout based on a threshold. Proposed rule: 60 days for orders with committed ARR > $250k OR TCV > $750k. Otherwise standard 30 days. This preserves predictability for our capacity planning.
- TFC fee: we can offer the pro‑rated service credit path as the primary option (customer credit applied to final invoice), with a cash fee only if credit is not acceptable. The attached TFC_fee_table.csv shows the credit tiers (e.g., >6 months remaining = 100% of remaining committed fees as credit; 3–6 months = 50%; <3 months = 25%), capped at six months.
- Offboarding: confirmed — we’ll add explicit language that export will be S3‑compatible, plus two 2‑hour migration consultations included.

Rishi (legal), does the MSA redline in §4 and the Order Form change to encode the enterprise carveout look reasonable from legal / risk? If you and Jordan’s team are aligned we can prepare a clean MSA and updated Order Form to push through DocuSign.

Ben

-----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Pike <jordan.pike@procureco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@procureco.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:45:22 -0800
Subject: RE: Term & Renewal language - cadence, notice windows, and TFC proposal

Thanks — reviewed the proposed carveouts. A couple of small legal asks to keep operational risk bounded:

1) Add a minimum notice floor for TFC-based offboarding: if a customer exercises TFC, Redwood gets the full notice period (90 days) to wind down and will continue to deliver per the Order Form through that period.
2) Cap the pro‑rated credit at the lesser of (a) six months of fees or (b) 50% of the remaining committed fees if customer has outstanding unpaid invoices. (We only surface the unpaid invoice clause in extraordinary cases.)
3) Add a short force‑majeure carveout that doesn’t extend auto‑renew timelines (we don’t want a month‑long outage to reset notice windows).

I’ll drop redlines into Redwood_MSA_v3_markup.pdf and an updated OrderForm_ProcureCo_DRAFT.xlsx. Ben/Marissa — if you prefer I can create the clean combined doc for signature after ProcureCo confirms the enterprise threshold.

Rishi Malhotra
General Counsel (Contracts) | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

-----
From: Jordan Pike <jordan.pike@procureco.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@procureco.com, legal@procureco.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Term & Renewal language - cadence, notice windows, and TFC proposal

Rishi / Ben —

This looks good from our procurement side and legal has green‑lit the credit approach with Rishi’s caps. Confirming ProcureCo will accept:
- 30‑day standard notice, 60‑day enterprise carveout at $250k ARR threshold;
- TFC via pro‑rated credit per the attached tiers with Rishi’s cap (lesser of six months or 50% with outstanding invoices clause);
- 90‑day TFC notice and continued service during the notice;
- 45‑day S3 export window + two migration consultations.

We’ll expect a clean MSA + Order Form for signature and a DocuSign link; please include language calling out the revenue threshold in the Order Form and mark it as an enterprise exception. Procurement aims to sign by EOM.

Jordan Pike
Director, Procurement | ProcureCo
jordan.pike@procureco.com

[Attachments: Redwood_MSA_v3_markup.pdf (redlines); OrderForm_ProcureCo_DRAFT.xlsx; TFC_fee_table.csv]
